release_notes:
Fix: false 'Another computer may be using the same station name' warning on a PC connected to the network two ways at once.

A computer plugged in by both Ethernet and Wi-Fi (both on the same network) could hear its OWN discovery announcement come back over the second adapter and mistake it for a different computer with the same station name. The result was a phantom duplicate at an IP address that didn't belong to any real computer, plus a repeating 'label already in use' loop in the connection log. Alerts still sent and received -- the warning was cosmetic but misleading.

Why it happened: the app worked out 'which IP addresses are me' (so it can ignore its own announcements) from only the primary network adapter, so an announcement looping back through a second adapter looked like a stranger.

The fix: each install now stamps a private per-session ID into its announcements and ignores any announcement carrying its own ID -- so a computer always recognizes itself no matter how many network adapters it has. Backward-compatible with stations still on older versions.

Immediate workaround if you see this warning before updating: use one network connection per computer (for example, turn off Wi-Fi on a PC that's on an Ethernet cable). The false warning clears within about 15 seconds.
